NutriVita Foods Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriVita Foods Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriVita Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, market share trends for major brands, revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, and gross margin analysis: drivers and trends.

First, regarding impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: As a leader in the Food & Beverage space—spanning packaged snacks, ready-to-drink beverages, dairy alternatives, and nutrition bars—we've navigated significant challenges this quarter, but our proactive strategies have helped preserve margins and build resilience. Input cost inflation drove a 9.2% year-over-year increase in our Cost of Goods Sold, exceeding our initial guidance of 7-8%, while supply chain disruptions inflated freight and logistics expenses by 22% from Q2. Together, these pressures compressed our adjusted gross margin by 210 basis points to 38.4%—still ahead of peers like Kellogg's at 35.2% or Mondelez at 37.1%, based on NielsenIQ data. That said, our pricing actions and operational measures offset about 65% of the gross impact, limiting EBITDA decline to just 4.1% year-over-year.

On input cost inflation, commodities made up 62% of the COGS rise. Agri-inputs have been volatile due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict disrupting Black Sea grain exports, La Niña weather patterns in South America, and biofuel demand. Grains and flours saw wheat prices up 28% to $9.50 per bushel per USDA index, affecting our tortilla chips and bakery snacks; corn rose 19% to $7.20 per bushel, hitting corn syrup in beverages and extruded snacks like our NutriVita Crunch bars. Edible oils jumped with palm oil up 32% from Indonesian curbs and El Niño forecasts, soybean oil up 24% from U.S. droughts, raising frying costs 15-18% for savory snacks, which are 22% of revenue. Sweeteners and cocoa also climbed—sugar 16% to $0.22 per pound from Brazilian delays, impacting RTD teas and energy drinks; cocoa spiked 45% to $4,200 per ton from West African failures, ballooning costs 12% for chocolate-coated nutrition bars. Dairy and proteins rose too, with fluid milk up 14% and whey powder 21% amid U.S. Midwest avian flu tightening supply.

Non-commodity costs added more: packaging resins like PET and aluminum up 11% on energy pass-throughs, energy costs up 25% from European squeezes affecting global LNG, and labor wages up 8% from U.S. port and warehouse pressures. Regionally, North America at 65% of sales saw 10.5% COGS inflation from grain volatility; EMEA 11.8% from energy shocks, with UK biscuits facing 30% wheat hikes post-Brexit; APAC moderated to 7.2% with rice stabilizing in India but palm oil hitting Indonesia; LATAM at 9.9% from sugar and coffee swings.

Supply chain disruptions amplified this, adding $142 million in one-offs or 80 basis points of margin pressure. Port and ocean freight issues from Red Sea tensions and Panama Canal droughts—water levels 20% below normal—caused 4-6 week delays, spiking spot rates 150% to $4,500 per FEU per Freightos Baltic Index, with 25% surcharges on Asian beverage imports. Trucking and rail bottlenecks included U.S. West Coast strikes idling 15% of shipments and EU rail down 18% from labor shortages, leading to 5x costlier air freight for plant-based proteins. Raw material shortages hit 12% stockout rate, worst in snacks from potato drops mirroring PepsiCo's Frito-Lay issues and cocoa rationing. North America took 55% of costs from East Coast port volatility; Europe 28% from Houthi reroutes; APAC eased to 12%; LATAM faced Argentine grain taxes.

This pushed inventory days to 52 from 45 year-over-year, with $28 million carrying costs. Our responses draw from proven playbooks like Nestle's supplier model and Unilever's digital twins: we've hedged 75% of 2024 grain volumes via Chicago Merc and ICE futures, capping at +5% vs. spot, with long-term deals from 18 suppliers like Kansas wheat co-ops and Brazilian Copersucar, cutting single-source risk 40%; cocoa forwards with Barry Callebaut secure 60% at 15% below spot. Pricing rose 7.8% year-over-year with elasticity of 0.4 in staples and 0.2 in premium—9% in snacks, 6.5% in beverages via shrinkflation. We've reformulated 20% palm oil to sunflower, saving 8%, and launched 15% more plant-based SKUs like almond-oat milks, now 18% of dairy portfolio growing 22%. Tech includes Blue Yonder AI for 92% forecast accuracy, slashing excess inventory 12%; IBM Food Trust blockchain for 65% traceability; $45 million nearshoring like a Texas tortilla plant online Q1 2025 cutting freight 30% and Mexico dairy hub. Regen-ag partnerships boost yields 10%, with 40% cocoa carbon-neutral.

These yielded $210 million in savings, covering 75% of headwinds, holding margins 380 basis points above 2022 lows. For Q4 and FY25, COGS inflation at 6-7%, disruptions normalizing 50% with Red Sea easing; guiding gross margin to 39.5% via 4-5% ASP, reformulations, $60 million automation capex. We're building resilient portfolios with 60% premium/health revenue, vertical integration like potato JVs, and AI networks, backed by 2.2x net debt/EBITDA and $1.2 billion liquidity.

Second, concerning e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: E-commerce has been central to our digital strategy as online grocery penetration hits 18% in the U.S. per Nielsen, up from 5% pre-pandemic. Q3 e-commerce sales hit $285 million, up 38% organically and 42% reported—our 11th straight double-digit quarter. At 10.2% of $2.8 billion total net revenue, it's up from 7.1% prior year and double three years ago; over 22% of direct-to-consumer excluding wholesale.

By category, Health & Wellness led with 52% growth in organic protein shakes like VitaPro and plant-based bars, via digital marketing and subscriptions. Beverages like QuenchZero low-cal sodas and functional waters grew 35%; ready-to-eat grain bowls 28% from meal kits. Average order value rose 12% to $48 with AI cross-selling boosting baskets 15%. North America at 68% or $194 million grew 45% via Amazon Fresh, Instacart, Walmart+; our VitaShop app hit 4.2 million monthly users, conversion to 4.8% with Shopify-like AI. EMEA $52 million up 25%, addressing packaging regs with recyclable pouches for EuroFit snacks per EU directives. APAC $39 million exploded 65% via Tmall, JD.com, Shopee for K-pop functional drinks at double U.S. AOV.

We've spent $150 million on infrastructure like a $75 million Reno fulfillment center with Ocado robotics, cutting costs 22% to 14% of revenue, on-time delivery 98%. Headless commerce and AR features integrate marketplaces; Snowflake CDP with 15 million loyalty data improves turnover 30%, stockouts under 2% for VitaPro. E-commerce margins hit 42.5%, +240 bps over company 38.2%, from low slotting and subscriptions at 35% of sales, churn <5%. Packaging 75% recyclable per Mintel. FY24 e-commerce $1.15 billion or 10.5%; Q4 40-45%; targeting 20% mix by FY27 with $200 million capex and M&A like Keurig's Ghost.

Third, in terms of impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: With over 55% of $2.8 billion quarterly revenue international—from snacks like NutriVita Crunch nut bars, AquaFizz energy waters, plant-based dairy—FX was a $92 million headwind, 330 basis points drag on reported growth to 4.2% vs. 7.5% constant currency. USD strengthened 4.8% trade-weighted per Fed index, like PepsiCo and Nestlé's 200-300 bps drags.

Europe (28% revenue) saw euro down 5.2%, $45 million hit or -4.1%; TasteCrunch-like exports to Germany/UK grew volumes but flat reported; EuroSpring waters up 6% locally. APAC (15%) $28 million headwind (-3.8%) from yen -7.1% and rupee softening, but constant 12% from China/Indonesia RTD teas. LATAM/emerging (12%) $19 million (-2.9%) from Brazil real -6.3%, Turkish lira; volumes +9% on health products, offset by Argentina pricing. Australian dollar gave $2 million tailwind.

Trends follow 2023's 10%+ USD strength from rate hikes, FX volatility at 15-year highs per Bloomberg from Ukraine and Red Sea. Hedges: 85% coverage layered—70% forwards, 20% collars, 10% swaps—at 3.2% premium; 92% Euro/yen inflows, 75% Q3-Q4 neutralizing 200 bps. Natural hedges: 65% local sourcing like Brazil nuts, Vietnam/Mexico plants $150 million capex. AI pricing from PROS passes 60-70% devals; Europe promos +150 bps mix.

We're leaning into health trends (+18% plant-based per NielsenIQ), local production like India nuts, Alibaba for China; target FX <40% revenue by 2027 via stable M&A. Constant currency shows brand strength for mid-single-digit growth.

Fourth, looking at market share trends for major brands: These trends highlight our portfolio's resilience per Nielsen, IRI, Circana data—net +120 bps dollar/unit share year-over-year, beating category -0.5%, from velocity in functional beverages and better-for-you snacks amid indulgent declines.

Zest Cola, challenging Coke/Pepsi, gained 1.8% to 27.2% North America dollar share—11th quarter—via Zero Regret low-cal at 42% volume; full-sugar category -3.2%. APAC +2.4% to 15.8% China via Alibaba/JD lychee flavors. HydroBoost hydration +3.1% to 22.4% global with plant-based electrolytes (-25% sodium, $45 million R&D); Europe +18% units to 19.7% despite sugar taxes; LATAM ACV 68% +5 via JDE cross-merch.

CrunchWave kettle chips held 31.5% U.S. share +90 bps YoY, 52% shelf; WaveLite health crisps (10g protein) 8.2% in $4.2 billion sub-category vs. Popchips/Quinn, +25% penetration. EMEA +0.7% tempered by Nutri-Score, accelerating palm-free 95% traceable via IBM. NutriSip oat milk +2.6% to 14.3% North America on 12% category growth, enzyme tech +22% taste preference vs. Oatly/Chobani; Australia 4.1%.

15% of $2.8 billion marketing to DTC digital, 28% ROI influencers like Celsius. ACV 92%, velocity +4% via Uber Eats/DoorDash. Q4 +80-100 bps expected; reshaping categories with innovation, agility.

Fifth, reviewing revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Following Q3 strength—7.2% organic revenue, +120 bps adjusted gross to 36.8%, +9% EPS to $1.28—we're reaffirming the midpoint for FY24 while raising high-end for EPS/FCF, on category momentum, cost management, supply chain wins.

Organic net revenue 6-8%: 4% volume, 3% price; Nutrition & Health strong like Chobani/Beyond despite impulse softness. Adjusted gross expansion 150-200 bps (up midpoint) from -15% commodities (wheat -12%, dairy -8%, oils stable), 85% hedges, $75 million Core4 AI procurement savings like Cargill.

Operating margin 12.5-13.5%, +75-100 bps; SG&A 22% via zero-based, Elevate $150 million savings automating route-to-market. EPS $5.10-5.30 (raised high-end), +$0.05 interest tailwind from $500 million refinance 4.2% vs. 5.8%, 24% tax; ex-$0.10 Q4 charge. FCF $1.1-1.2 billion (95-105% net income), capex $650 million on Mexico aseptic for protein shakes +50 million cases.

North America 7-9% organic, +1.2 snack share via CoreCrunch, 18% promo volume. EMEA 4-6%, plant-based +15% at Tesco/Carrefour, local oats vs. FX. APAC/LATAM high-single, China e-com +12%, Brazil +10% hydration.

NutriCore 2025: divest $300 million low-margin dairy for functional M&A like Pepsi Poppi; SAP S/4HANA Q3 for 30% less stockouts; regen-ag 40% wheat -12% Scope 3. At-home +2%, away-from-home 35% on QSR recovery. 75% FCF to dividends/$800 million buybacks; $2.5 billion liquidity, 2.2x debt/EBITDA.

Sixth, analyzing gross margin analysis: drivers and trends: Q3 consolidated gross margin 38.5%, +130 bps sequential from 37.2% Q2, +220 bps YoY reported/+250 constant—sixth straight expansion, trailing four-quarter 37.8% beating 36-38% target and peers like Kellogg/General Mills.

Pricing +320 bps from 8-10% increases no volume loss on premium equity; PureHarvest organics +12% price/5% volume like Mondelez. Mix +150 bps: premium/health 42% from 35%, +double-digit plant-based GreenWave; pruned 15% value snacks +2.5 mix.

Input inflation -180 bps: dairy +15%, sugar +20% Brazil, oils +12% Indonesia; transport/packaging -50 bps Red Sea +25% freight. Efficiencies +280 bps: 70% hedges $45 million wheat/corn/cocoa like Hershey; LeanFreshaura +4% yields Midwest cereals.

J-curve from FY22 34.1% low; FY23 +400 bps; FY24 +300 bps, Q3 guide 39.0-39.5%. Sequential from dairy comps, Q1 automation; beverages 42.1% +350 bps (35% revenue), snacks 36.8% +180, prepared 34.2%.

North America 40.1% +280 bps scale/proximity; EMEA 36.5% -120 bps energy/EU deforestation; APAC 37.9% +400 bps China plant-based; LATAM 35.2% Argentina/Brazil offset by Mexico solar.

Global Procurement 2.0 $120 million YTD AI/waste -7%; $250 million vertical like Côte d'Ivoire cocoa +300 bps; regen-ag -15% fertilizer/EU credits; robotics 12% throughput +50-75 bps. FY24 38.5-39.0%, +100-150 tailwinds vs. 5-7% inflation; risks El Niño/tariffs. Functional RTDs/M&A derisk; 20%+ EBITDA by FY26.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.8 billion, representing a 6% increase year-over-year on a reported basis, or 9.5% on a constant currency basis. Gross margin was 38.5%, impacted by input inflation partially offset by pricing and efficiencies. Operating income was $385 million, and earnings per share were $1.32. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic net revenue growth of 6% to 8%, adjusted gross margin expansion of 150 to 200 basis points, adjusted EPS of $5.10 to $5.30, and free cash flow of $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, John. As I outlined earlier, input inflation hit COGS 9.2% year-over-year, driven by grains, oils, and dairy, but our hedging, pricing at 7.8%, and reformulations offset 65%, preserving industry-leading margins. We're seeing moderation ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new plant-based protein shakes and what is the expected impact on revenue?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our new VitaPro plant-based shakes build on 52% e-commerce growth in Health & Wellness, with enzyme tech for better texture and subscriptions driving recurring revenue. We expect them to add $150 million in FY25 revenue, accelerating 12-15% category growth and boosting direct-to-consumer mix.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Mike Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Mike. Disruptions added $142 million from freight spikes and stockouts, but nearshoring like our Texas plant, AI forecasting to 92% accuracy, and blockchain traceability have normalized impacts 50% already. Inventory safety stocking is strategic, with Q4 efficiencies from Red Sea easing.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please proceed.

Sarah Patel (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thanks, Sarah. Q4 should see COGS inflation taper to 6-7%, e-commerce accelerate 40-45%, and gross margins to 39.5% from pricing and mix. We're on track for full-year guidance midpoints or better, with constant currency momentum offsetting FX, focused on health trends and share gains.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Thompson for closing remarks.

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriVita Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
